persons.name: Bora Özkent
persons.digest:
Bora Özkent explains how personal AI agents — Meta's **Muse** and the Grok agent he uses heavily himself — are set to transform daily life and shopping, saying he has handed off everything from trip planning to email management to his agent. He says the most concrete investment impact of this shift is rising inference-compute demand, which is why CPU makers like **Intel**, **AMD** and **ARM** have gained value; he adds **Nvidia** could also benefit from rising demand, though it isn't as dominant in inference as in training. He cites Deloitte's estimate of $35-45 billion in agent-subscription revenue by 2030 and McKinsey's estimate that agent-managed shopping could reach $3-5 trillion.

On individual companies, he thinks **Meta** could profit from Muse subscriptions and commissions but that its valuation is rising fast; **Google**'s ad revenue could shrink since agents won't watch ads; and **Microsoft** could see Azure grow while software-license revenue bleeds. He doesn't think **Amazon**'s move to block Muse from shopping is smart, and says it bothers him as an Amazon investor. He thinks **Salesforce** and **Booking.com** could be hurt by their human/intermediary-based models, while **Akamai** still has room to run after its 20% jump on the Anthropic deal, and that **Okta**, **JFrog**, **Rambus**, **nVent** and **DigitalOcean** are lesser-known names that could benefit from the agent economy (identity verification, software security, memory, cooling, cloud infrastructure).

items.title: If Everyone Has an AI Agent, Which Stocks Get Stronger?
items.summary: Using Meta's **Muse** and the Grok agent he uses himself as examples, Bora Özkent explains how personal AI agents are changing daily life, from trip planning to shopping, email management and subscription tracking. He says agents run on large data centers behind the scenes, that inference compute will reach two-thirds of total AI compute in 2026, and that this is lifting the value of CPU makers **Intel**, **AMD** and **ARM**. He cites Deloitte's estimate of $35-45 billion in agent-subscription revenue and McKinsey's estimate that agents could manage $3-5 trillion in shopping by 2030, against which software and ad companies could lose roughly $234 billion in revenue. He says **Meta** could profit from subscriptions and commissions but its valuation is rising fast; **Google**'s ad revenue, **Microsoft**'s software-license revenue, and **Salesforce**'s and **Booking.com**'s intermediary/seat-based models are all at risk. He says he doesn't find **Amazon**'s decision to block Muse from shopping smart, and that it bothers him as an Amazon investor. He assesses that **Akamai** still has upside after its 20% rally on the Anthropic deal, and that **Okta**, **JFrog**, **Rambus**, **nVent** and **DigitalOcean** are lesser-known names that could benefit from the agent economy.

items.summary: He argued he doesn't accept the 1-million-TL threshold, that PPFs are deposit-like products, that investors shouldn't pay for the regulator's negligence, and that everyone should be paid in full immediately.

persons.name: WallStDiaries
persons.digest: WallStDiaries wrote today that the US 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.44%, its highest since 2004, that the mortgage rate topped 7% for the first time since January 2025, and that Michigan consumer confidence was expected to fall while inflation expectations rise. It reported that US and Iranian negotiators are discussing lifting the blockade in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with neither side wanting to give up leverage first. It shared that **Nvidia (NVDA)** chip demand is rising via xAI's Colossus 2 center, that China is reviewing **Broadcom (AVGO)** network switches, and that First Solar fell more than 10% on financing pressure. It also added that Novo Nordisk signed a €1.17 billion deal with Nanexa and that Solana leads crypto ETF volume with a 46% share.

items.title: Today's US data calendar and an inflation-expectations warning
items.summary: It wrote that Michigan consumer confidence was expected to fall from 51.7 to 47.6, and that the real key data point would be the embedded inflation-expectations line, which could feed bond yields.

items.title: Costco's Q4 results came in strong
items.summary: It reported that Costco's net sales rose 11.2% and operating income rose 13.8%, that membership revenue was a source of stability, while gross margin slipped 11 basis points.

assets.note: Net sales up 11.2%, operating income up 13.8%; gross margin slipped slightly.

items.title: US 30-year Treasury yield at its highest since 2004
items.summary: It wrote that the 30-year US Treasury yield hit 5.44%, its highest since 2004, which is not a tailwind for equity multiples or borrowing costs.

items.title: Jobless claims stayed low
items.summary: It wrote that initial jobless claims came in below expectations, that the labor market isn't loosening, and that this narrows the Fed's room to maneuver.

items.title: Nvidia chip demand doubling via Colossus 2

assets.note: xAI aims to double the chip count at Colossus 2 by year-end.

items.title: $85,000 mining-cost threshold important for Bitcoin
items.summary: It wrote that an average Bitcoin mining cost around $85,000 could make that level an important reference for supply-side stress.

assets.note: The $85,000 mining-cost level is being watched as an important reference.

items.title: Solana leads crypto ETF volume
items.summary: It wrote that Solana leads with a 46% share of non-BTC/ETH spot ETF volume, showing capital spreading into a broader crypto basket.

items.title: Novo Nordisk's $1.17B licensing deal with Nanexa

items.summary: It wrote that the 5% threshold in US Treasury yields is being priced as a permanent new regime, which will put equity valuations and debt-rollover appetite through a tougher test.

items.summary: It wrote that Bitget's CEO confirmed the cyberattack and that the $351.6 million loss will be fully covered by the $464 million protection fund.

items.title: First Solar fell sharply on financing pressure
items.summary: It wrote that peaking bond yields and rising borrowing costs sent First Solar down more than 10% to a 52-week low.

assets.note: US pressure to restrict exports to China is a risk to ASML's market share.

items.title: China reviewing Broadcom network switches
items.summary: It wrote that China is reviewing the use of Broadcom network switches in state-backed data centers, where this hardware holds up to 90% share in some deployments.

assets.note: China reviewing Broadcom network switches in state-backed data centers puts Chinese revenue at risk.

items.title: 30-year mortgage rate tops 7%
items.summary: It wrote that the US 30-year fixed mortgage rate topped 7% for the first time since January 2025, reaching 7.03%, and that housing demand is under pressure.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz bargaining on the table
items.summary: It wrote that US and Iranian negotiators are discussing lifting the blockade in exchange for Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with neither side wanting to give up leverage first.

persons.name: FinancewithIzzy
persons.digest: FinancewithIzzy read the seating at the Trump-Xi state dinner — with Elon Musk, Jensen Huang and Tim Cook at the same table — as an important signal for AI, chips and the US-China power balance. He called **Cipher Digital (CIFR)**'s extension of the Barber Lake deal to 20 years, pushing total revenue above $9 billion, very good news, but noted the stock still fell 2.18%, showing the market is now looking past company news to other factors like liquidity, rates and valuation. He said **AMD**'s path after 5 years of sideways trading is a reminder of the value of patient investors who trust the fundamental story.

items.title: CIFR and Neo Cloud sold off despite strong news

persons.name: wallstengine
persons.digest: wallstengine reported today that Tesla opened its new Semi truck factory in Nevada (capacity ~1,000 trucks/week) and ramped Optimus production from dozens to hundreds of units per quarter, and that Microsoft is reframing Copilot as the 'OS for work' with Satya Nadella saying the agent market could grow bigger than the cloud business. It wrote that SK Hynix is weighing a $150 billion IPO valuation for Solidigm, potentially the largest US semiconductor IPO ever, and that Cipher Digital extended its Barber Lake data-center deal to 20 years, pushing revenue above $9 billion. It shared that Oura's IPO drew roughly 4x oversubscription, that BofA cut Nike's price target from $47 to $30, and that a US court upheld Anthropic's Pentagon contracting ban. It also added that Meta's Muse partnered with Plaid and that Canaccord raised Meta's price target to $950.
